pr_title: Refactor fill models to not depend on fee models
pr_body:
<!--- Provide a general summary of your changes in the Title above -->

#### Description
<!--- Describe your changes in detail -->
Invocation of `IFeeModel` has been moved from the `IFillModel` implementations (and `IOptionExerciseModel` to the `BacktestingBrokerage` (or any other invoker of `IFillModel`). `BacktestingBrokerage` has also been updated to invoke `IFeeModel` for orders that have been completely filled, which is in-line with the current implementations of `IFillModel`.

We may want to remove the restriction of only invoking fee models on completely filled orders to support partial fees (common in crypto exchanges) as well as order submission fees (less common, but some brokerages charge these). For this PR, maintaining existing functionality was the primary concern as this is only a refactor of existing method call hierarchies. 

#### Related Issue
<!--- This project only accepts pull requests related to open issues -->
<!--- If suggesting a new feature or change, please discuss it in an issue first -->
<!--- If fixing a bug, there should be an issue describing it with steps to reproduce -->
<!--- Please link to the issue here: -->
Closes #2567 

#### Motivation and Context
<!--- Why is this change required? What problem does it solve? -->
A recent attempt to improve the implementation of `IFeeModel` revealed a dependency issue between `IFillModel` and `IFeeModel`. Separating the invocation of `IFeeModel` from those who implement `IFillModel` will resolve this dependency issue. The assumption here is that user models should be directly invoked from LEAN infrastructure rather than from other models. By maintaining this invocation pattern, we free ourselves from requiring user models to manage dependencies that _other_ user models may require (now or in the future). 

#### Requires Documentation Change
<!--- Please indicate if these changes will require updates to documentation, and if so, specify what changes are required -->
YES! We should update our documentation regarding custom `IFillModel` implementations to use the `FillModel` base class as well as to **not** compute an order fee.

#### How Has This Been Tested?
<!--- Please describe in detail how you tested your changes. -->
<!--- Include details of your testing environment, and the tests you ran to -->
<!--- see how your change affects other areas of the code, etc. -->
These changes are extensively covered by unit tests. Existing `ImmediateFillModelTests` were updated to confirm zero fees were returned.

pr_comments:
Shame on me for using travis as a test runner :/

Investigating unexpected test failures.

RESOLUTION: Errors came from incorrectly refactoring out fee computation due to a removed if block. Setting the order event's fill quantity was moved to within the various switch statements to ensure all conditions are properly met before setting the filled quantity.

<!--- This template provides sections for bugs and features. Please delete any irrelevant sections before submitting -->

#### Expected Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the behavior you expect to see for your case. -->
Fill models don't have dependency on fee models

#### Actual Behavior
<!--- Required. Describe the actual behavior for your case. -->
Fill models are expected to invoke fee models directly.

#### Potential Solution
<!--- Optional. Describe any potential solutions and/or thoughts as to what may be causing the difference between expected and actual behavior. -->
Invoke fill and fee models separately and compose the result. In order to maintain backwards compatibility, confirm that the fee hasn't been computed before computing and applying the fee.

review_comments: What are your thoughts about checking whether or not `fill` is the new base class `FillModel` or a derivative of it, versus checking for order fee 0? Maybe using `IsAssignableFrom`
great idea, since it's definitely possible that a custom `IFillModel` implemented zero fees explicitly and in contradiction to the configured `IFeeModel` -- I'll make this change 👍

after more thought, I'm not sure this will be great as it would cause a bug if a user directly implements the `IFillModel` interface, for example, in python. Now, we could also check for the python type (which doesn't subclass `FillModel`), but I think for now checking zero is sufficient. I'll add a note that we should remove the check in 6 months
